adoption.body: Current AI use increased slightly to 23.8% of businesses, while expected use within six months rose to 27.6%. The gap narrowed to 3.8 percentage points, putting stated near-term intentions closer to reported deployment. Adoption remains uneven: the leading sector's current-use reading rose materially to 49.0%, more than twice the all-business rate.
adoption.headline: Business AI use rises as the near-term intention gap narrows

compute.body: Computer and peripheral-equipment output grew 9.2%, with capacity utilization at 81.7%. Semiconductor and electronic-component output grew 11.5%, but utilization was lower at 72.2%. Output is rising in both industries, while the utilization gap indicates different pressure on installed capacity.
compute.headline: Compute output is growing under different capacity conditions

macro.body: Investor support remains constructive but selective. The AI Equity Index edged up to 36.7 and the median one-year return reached 13.7%, while the share of covered companies with positive one-year returns fell to 62.7%. The Financial Times reported that robust AI spending was supporting expectations for another strong U.S. earnings season, but the return data still show uneven participation. Financing is also mixed: the NFCI is -0.49 after a 0.02 rise over three months, while borrower strain is 26.0 and lender strain is -13.5. Computer and peripheral-equipment output is growing 9.2%, and semiconductor and electronic-component output 11.5%. Commercial electricity demand growth of 3.1% is also outpacing total retail demand growth of 1.2%. These are broad industry measures rather than AI-only series, but they describe an expanding hardware and power context for the buildout. Grid execution remains separate from the size of the pipeline: only 24.2% of the active interconnection queue is in executed-agreement or construction stages. Utility Dive reported that MISO proposed fast-track studies for large loads and generation. The proposal is a procedural change, not delivered capacity. Broader diffusion is less evident in labor and business use. Only one tracked AI-linked labor channel has positive employment growth, led by power and communication construction at 0.8%, and two have positive real-earnings growth. CNBC reported surging Wall Street AI hiring, which provides a sector-specific contrast rather than evidence of broad acceleration. Current AI use is reported by 23.8% of businesses, with 27.6% expecting use within six months. These measures leave diffusion through firms and the labor market incomplete even as selected industries report strong AI hiring.
macro.headline: Market support and physical expansion coexist with narrow labor gains

market.body: The AI Equity Index edged up to 36.7 and the median one-year return rose to 13.7%, but the share of covered companies with positive one-year returns slipped to 62.7%. Gains therefore persisted without becoming more broadly distributed. The Financial Times reported that robust AI spending was supporting expectations for another strong U.S. earnings season. That strengthens the near-term earnings narrative, but it does not show that results are improving across the full set of covered companies.
market.headline: AI shares advance without broader participation

power.body: Commercial electricity demand is growing 3.1%, versus 1.2% for total retail demand, while retail prices are up 4.4%. Net planned generation additions total 225.2 GW through the pipeline horizon. Utility Dive reported that MISO proposed a fast-track study process for large loads and generation. The proposal concerns study timing; it does not establish when planned capacity will connect or how local supply-demand balances will change.
power.headline: Commercial demand leads electricity growth as faster grid studies are proposed

workforce.body: Only one tracked AI-linked labor channel has positive employment growth. Power and communication construction leads at 0.8%, while two channels have positive real-earnings growth. CNBC reported that Wall Street AI hiring is surging, providing a sector-specific counterpoint. The report does not amount to broad acceleration across the tracked labor channels.
workforce.headline: Sector-specific AI hiring contrasts with narrow tracked job growth

editorial_briefing.style_reference: AI Macro is a research platform that examines the development of the U.S. AI economy from capital investment and physical construction through deployment, adoption, and economic results. It uses publicly available data to relate corporate and market activity to the physical systems required to support the buildout. It evaluates the extent to which that investment produces durable economic value and how its effects are transmitted through the broader U.S. economy.

body.text: The AI Equity Index slipped to 36.1 and average sector trading pressure fell to 49.7. The share of covered companies with positive one-year returns declined to 61.8%, while the median one-year return fell more materially to 12.0%. A late-September report described gains in AI stocks despite weak index trading, a point-in-time example of selective strength rather than evidence that participation has widened.

Computer and peripheral-equipment output is growing 9.2%, with utilization at 81.7%. Semiconductor and electronic-component output is growing faster, at 11.5%, but utilization is lower at 72.2%, so the two industries continue to expand under different capacity conditions. Recent semiconductor trade reporting focused on characterization and testing in advanced packaging and on catching hybrid-bonding defects before they become costly failures. Those reports concern production control at specific process stages; they do not establish that aggregate semiconductor capacity is tight.

headline.text: Compute output grows while packaging execution draws attention

body.text: Businesses expecting to use AI within six months edged up to 27.7%. The expected-minus-current gap widened slightly to 3.9 percentage points, while the leading sector’s current-use reading reached 50.2%. Current-use readings now cover every BTOS sector, making cross-sector comparisons more complete. Separately, the 2025 Small Business Credit Survey found that 46% of firms with employees said the business or its employees used AI tools, and another 15% planned to adopt them within a year. The surveys use different populations and horizons, so their levels should not be treated as directly comparable.

headline.text: Near-term AI-use expectations inch higher as leading-sector use passes 50%

body.text: Only one tracked AI-linked labor channel has positive employment growth, led by power and communication construction at 0.8%; two channels have positive real-earnings growth. In a separate survey, 46% of firms with employees reported that the business or its employees used AI tools, and another 15% planned adoption within a year. These measures cover different populations, but they show substantial reported tool use coexisting with limited employment breadth. They do not establish whether AI is raising or reducing overall employment.

headline.text: Reported AI use contrasts with narrow employment growth
Physical expansion and business adoption remain more visible than broad labor gains

paragraphs.text: The physical setting for AI investment continues to expand, though the underlying industry series are not AI-specific. Computer and peripheral-equipment output is growing 9.2%, and semiconductor and electronic-component output 11.5%. Commercial electricity demand is up 3.1%, ahead of total retail demand at 1.2%, and the planned generation pipeline shows 225.2 GW of net additions. Delivery remains more uncertain than the pipeline headline: 2,061 GW is waiting in active interconnection queues, only 24.2% is in executed-agreement or construction stages, and just 13% of the 2000–2020 queue cohort reached operation.

Adoption is advancing, but not uniformly. Businesses expecting AI use within six months edged up to 27.7%, only 3.9 percentage points above current use, while the leading sector’s current-use reading reached 50.2%. The Small Business Credit Survey separately found that 46% of firms with employees reported use by the business or its employees and another 15% planned adoption within a year. These surveys are not directly comparable. Meanwhile, only one tracked AI-linked labor channel has positive employment growth, led by power and communication construction at 0.8%, and two have positive real-earnings growth. Reported use therefore coexists with narrow labor-market breadth, without establishing AI’s effect on overall employment.

Equity markets are offering less confirmation of a broadening cycle. The AI Equity Index slipped to 36.1, the share of covered companies with positive one-year returns declined to 61.8%, and the median one-year return fell materially to 12.0%. Operating cash flow still covers current capital expenditure by 1.42 times, while cash reserves amount to 0.96 years of current capital expenditure. Current spending therefore has internal funding coverage, but less than a full year of capital expenditure in cash reserves. Together with weaker equity breadth, the figures describe a buildout continuing without uniformly stronger market support.

Use only the findings and recent developments in the supplied briefing. Decide what matters, connect related evidence when the relationship is supported, and explain it in clear, natural English for an intelligent general reader. Prioritize significance over coverage. It is fine for the evidence to be mixed. Do not force unrelated facts into one story.

The style reference shows the desired level of restraint, specificity, and sentence construction. Match those qualities without copying its wording. Write like a careful human analyst. Use concrete subjects and verbs. Avoid rhetorical gimmicks and artificial-sounding transitions. Do not mention the prompt, the briefing, evidence IDs, validation, methodology, or the writing process.

On a normal update, candidate_domains identifies sections that may deserve replacement. Update only the domain Reads for which you can write something materially more useful than the prior publication; you may return no domain Reads when none deserves replacement. On a bootstrap publication, write every candidate domain because no prior Read exists. Always write one new Macro Read that explains the most important current story across the platform in two to four coherent paragraphs.

Do not inventory every supplied metric or news item. Use a number only when it helps the reader understand magnitude. Use recent developments when they materially sharpen the interpretation of the measured findings. Treat news reports as reported developments, not as proof of a broader causal claim.

Attach only the fact_ids and event_ids that actually support each passage. Those IDs are citations for the application and must never appear in the prose. Do not invent numbers, facts, events, causes, or forecasts.

Return only the structured response.

Recent semiconductor trade reporting focused on characterization and testing in advanced packaging and on catching hybrid-bonding defects before they become costly failures. Those reports concern production control at specific process stages; they do not establish that aggregate semiconductor capacity is tight.
